user.title: Add your Anova cooker
user.description:
How should Home Assistant talk to the cooker?

- **Bluetooth (direct)** works straight away, with a Bluetooth adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy within range.
- **Wi-Fi (local server)** puts the cooker on your Wi-Fi so distance stops mattering. Home Assistant takes the place of Anova's cloud, so there is no account and no Anova app involved. You need the cooker within a few metres of Home Assistant once, for this setup.

data_description.address: The list shows the cookers Home Assistant can hear over Bluetooth. If it is empty, the cooker is not switched on or is out of range; then enter its address, printed on the label underneath the cooker, instead.

bluetooth_confirm.title: Set up {name}?
bluetooth_confirm.description:
Home Assistant found {name} over Bluetooth. Choose how Home Assistant talks to it:

- **Wi-Fi (local server)** puts the cooker on your Wi-Fi so distance stops mattering: Home Assistant takes the place of Anova's cloud, with no account and no Anova app. You need the cooker within a few metres of Home Assistant once, for this setup.
- **Bluetooth (direct)** works straight away, as long as a Bluetooth adapter or ESPHome Bluetooth proxy stays in range. Nothing is written to the cooker; you can remove this integration at any time.

wifi.title: Give the cooker your Wi-Fi
wifi.description:
Enter the network the cooker should use. It supports **2.4 GHz** only, and cannot join a network name that contains a space.

Home Assistant then writes three settings over Bluetooth: a fresh security key, its own address ({host}:{port}) and this Wi-Fi network. The cooker stores them and keeps them after a reboot. Only the Anova app can undo them.

Close the Anova app first: the cooker accepts one Bluetooth connection at a time.

When the settings are written, the cooker signs off Bluetooth and joins your Wi-Fi. Give it about a minute to call Home Assistant, then it appears as a working cooker. If a minute has passed, unplug the cooker somewhere you can see it, plug it back in and run this setup once more.

error.not_found: The cooker did not answer over Bluetooth. Is it plugged in and switched on? The ring should be lit.
error.unsupported: The cooker answered, but not in a way this integration understands. Please report this with your firmware version.
error.wifi_credentials_invalid: The cooker cannot use this network: its name may not contain a space, and the password must be 8 to 63 characters.
error.provision_failed: The settings could not be written. Keep the cooker within a few metres of Home Assistant, close the Anova app, and check the log for the reason.

abort.already_configured: This cooker is already set up.
abort.not_found: The cooker is not in range. Switch it on and try again.
abort.unsupported: This device did not answer as an Anova cooker.
abort.bluetooth_not_available: No connectable Bluetooth adapter found. Add one, or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy, and try again.
